limitations_and_boundaries: GBC detection probability is lower in BMDCs (60%) due to lower cell complexity; increases to 70% after filtering low-complexity cells.
On-target reduction detection is affected by target expression level in WT cells, capture efficiency, and incomplete nonsense-mediated decay.
Current Perturb-seq scale is suitable for targeted screens; genome-wide or combinatorial screens require increased cell throughput and computational scaling.
Probability of detecting all perturbations and their effects scales exponentially with the order of perturbations.
Linear model may not capture all nonlinearities; interaction terms are limited to those included.

research_questions.statement: How can Perturb-seq be used to dissect transcriptional effects of genetic perturbations at single-cell resolution?

provenance.text_excerpt: A technology combining single-cell RNA sequencing with CRISPR-based perturbations termed Perturb-seq makes analyzing complex phenotypes at a large scale possible

claims.statement: Perturb-seq combines pooled CRISPR screens with single-cell RNA-seq to dissect transcriptional effects of genetic perturbations at scale.

provenance.text_excerpt: At its current scale, Perturb-seq can be readily applied for targeted screens of a subset of genes of interest and their interactions... claims.statement: Perturb-seq can scale to larger screens: genome-wide or combinatorial screens are feasible with increasing cell throughput and computational bandwidth, and future improvements (e.g., Cpf1, lineage tracing) are compatible.

methods.name: Perturb-seq
methods.protocol_description: A method combining pooled CRISPR screen with single-cell RNA-seq readout. Lentiviral vector delivers sgRNA and an expressed GBC. Cells are transduced, selected (FACS or antibiotics), grown/differentiated/stimulated, then scRNA-seq performed in a single pool. GBCs are enriched via PCR after whole transcriptome amplification. MOI can be varied for single or combinatorial perturbations.

methods.name: MIMOSCA computational framework
methods.protocol_description: A regularized linear model (elastic net) predicting each gene's expression as a function of guide effects, technical covariates (number of transcripts, detection probability), and biological covariates (cell state, subtype). Permutation-based significance testing. Iterative re-assignment of perturbation probability to cells. Can incorporate interaction terms for genetic interactions or cell-state-specific effects.

methods.name: Cell state definition
methods.protocol_description: Cell states defined from unperturbed cells by selecting variable genes via Loess regression on coefficient of variation vs. mean expression, normalizing to 10,000 transcripts, log2 transformation, Z-transformation, randomized PCA retaining top ~10 components, clustering with Infomap, and iterative merging until no pairwise clusters have <100 differentially expressed genes (Welch's t test, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR).

methods.name: Cell cycle regulator Perturb-seq analysis
methods.protocol_description: Used Perturb-seq with 10 cell-cycle regulators in K562 cells; analyzed effects on cell-cycle states and gene expression, revealing distinct profiles associated with similar fitness effects and mitotic arrest.

results.value_raw_text: 94% (92%–96%) detection probability in K562 TF pool (MOI 0.63); 98% in cell-cycle pool (MOI 0.35); 60% in BMDCs at 3 hr (MOI 1.4), increasing to 70% after filtering low-complexity cells.

results.value_raw_text: Fitness effects of sgRNAs are assessed by fold change in abundance compared to initial pool, with significance determined via a Bayesian model using binomial p value and Bonferroni correction.
